title: Turkey-Pakistan-Saudi Mecca Pact Takes Effect, US Forces Respond to RAF Lakenheath Drones, and B-21 Raider Releases First Weapon
subhead: Ankara enacted a trilateral collective-defense treaty alongside a Doha security accord, while suspected drones tested RAF Lakenheath and Northrop Grumman's B-21 Raider hit a key weapons-testing milestone.

sections.heading: Mecca Joint Defense Pact Enters Into Force Alongside Qatar Accord
sections.body:
The Mecca Joint Defense Agreement among Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia took legal effect on November 14 following publication in Turkey's Official Gazette, according to BBC Türkçe, Milliyet, and Ekonomim. Under the treaty, an armed attack against one member is treated as an attack against all three.

In parallel, Al Jazeera and Ekonomim reported that Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defense agreement pledging joint action against external attacks, while Defense News noted Turkey and Egypt are weighing joint naval shipbuilding projects.
sections.whyItMatters: Ankara is binding key regional partners into formal collective-defense and naval-industrial commitments.

sections.heading: Suspected Drones Trigger Alert at RAF Lakenheath
sections.body:
The War Zone, Le Monde, and SCMP reported that US Air Force security personnel responded on Friday evening to suspected unauthorized drone activity over RAF Lakenheath in England. Both the UK Ministry of Defence and a USAF spokesperson confirmed no personnel, aircraft, or infrastructure were harmed and declared the incident resolved.

The Times of Israel noted the scare comes after recent tanker evacuations from RAF Mildenhall and marks the third suspected drone incident near US warplanes in Britain in recent weeks.
sections.whyItMatters: Persistent small-drone activity near UK bases hosting American combat aircraft underscores ongoing counter-UAS vulnerabilities across NATO's rear areas.

sections.heading: B-21 Raider Releases First Weapon as USAF Adopts Force Design 2026
sections.body:
The War Zone reported that the B-21 Raider stealth bomber has released its first weapon, marking a major milestone as the US Air Force aims to declare the bomber operational next year. Meanwhile, Defense News reported the service adopted Force Design 2026, prioritizing artificial intelligence, autonomy, and integrated sensors.

In high-speed unmanned aviation, The War Zone also reported that startup Hermeus partnered with Northrop Grumman to develop operational very-high-speed military drones, while the USAF introduced the T-19A Kestrel aerobatic trainer.
sections.whyItMatters: The Air Force is pairing its next-generation stealth bomber rollout with autonomous sensor networks and high-speed unmanned platforms.

sections.heading: Poland Seeks Tomahawks as US Navy Eyes SSN(X) Drone Mothership
sections.body:
M5 Dergi reported that Poland submitted a formal request to Washington to procure Tomahawk cruise missiles and compatible launchers to bolster long-range precision strike capability. Simultaneously, the US Navy accelerated Tomahawk warhead production at China Lake, California to meet rising Raytheon demand.

Undersea, USNI News reported the Navy is finalizing alternatives for the SSN(X) nuclear attack submarine to serve as a faster mothership for undersea drones, while transferring two T38 Devil Ray unmanned surface vessels to the Philippine Marine Corps.
sections.whyItMatters: Allied demand for long-range strike munitions is rising alongside US Navy investments in unmanned surface and undersea payloads.

sections.heading: Belgium Orders 14 Blue Dome Radars as Italy Prioritizes GCAP
sections.body:
M5 Dergi reported that Belgium will procure 14 Thales GM200 MM/C radars for its Blue Dome integrated air and missile defense network to track drones, cruise missiles, and aircraft. Meanwhile, Defense News reported Italy increased spending on the sixth-generation GCAP fighter program while cutting army tank and fighting-vehicle budgets.

At sea, USNI News reported the Royal Navy will trial Northrop Grumman's Talon autonomous testbed off a Queen Elizabeth-class carrier in 2027, while Beretta unveiled the Italian-developed LIVET remote counter-drone turret mounting eight Benelli M4 shotguns.
sections.whyItMatters: European militaries are reallocating procurement budgets toward air-defense sensors, sixth-generation air combat, and carrier-based autonomy.

bottomLine: Collective-defense treaties in the Middle East, repeated drone scares over UK airbases, B-21 weapons testing, and European air-defense radar orders illustrate how allied forces are simultaneously hardening rear bases and accelerating long-range and autonomous capabilities.
sources: The War Zone, Defense News, USNI News, M5 Dergi, Le Monde, Times of Israel, SCMP, BBC Türkçe, Ekonomim, Al Jazeera
